hints: Cumulative frequency represents the total number of values less than or equal to a given boundary.
To find the number of journey times between $25$ and $45$ minutes, subtract the cumulative frequency at $25$ from the cumulative frequency at $45$.
walkthrough:
Use the cumulative frequency table to find the class frequency in the interval $25 < t \le 45$:
$$\text{Frequency} = \text{CF}(45) - \text{CF}(25)$$

Substitute the cumulative frequencies $\text{CF}(45) = 50$ and $\text{CF}(25) = 18$ from the table:
$$\text{Frequency} = 50 - 18 = 32$$

ai_rubric.Constructing Frequency Tables: Subtracts cumulative frequencies to obtain the required class frequency.

teacher_walkthrough: Look at the cumulative frequency table. The cumulative total up to 45 minutes is 50 people, and up to 25 minutes is 18 people.

Subtract the two cumulative frequencies to find how many people took between 25 and 45 minutes:
$$\text{Frequency} = 50 - 18 = 32\text{ people}$$

hints: Find the individual class frequencies by taking differences between consecutive cumulative frequencies.
Calculate the class width for each interval: $\text{upper limit} - \text{lower limit}$.
Use $\text{Frequency Density} = \dfrac{\text{Frequency}}{\text{Class Width}}$ to determine the height of each bar.
Draw adjoining bars spanning the exact class boundaries and clearly label both axes: 'Time (mins)' horizontally and 'Frequency density' vertically.
walkthrough:
Calculate the class frequency $f$, class width $w$, and frequency density $\text{FD} = \dfrac{f}{w}$ for each interval:
$$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|} \hline \text{Interval } (t) & \text{Cumulative Frequency} & \text{Class Frequency } (f) & \text{Class Width } (w) & \text{Frequency Density } (\text{FD}) \\ \hline 0 < t \le 10 & 0 & 0 & 10 & \frac{0}{10} = 0.0 \\ \hline 10 < t \le 25 & 18 & 18 - 0 = 18 & 25 - 10 = 15 & \frac{18}{15} = 1.2 \\ \hline 25 < t \le 45 & 50 & 50 - 18 = 32 & 45 - 25 = 20 & \frac{32}{20} = 1.6 \\ \hline 45 < t \le 60 & 59 & 59 - 50 = 9 & 60 - 45 = 15 & \frac{9}{15} = 0.6 \\ \hline 60 < t \le 80 & 63 & 63 - 59 = 4 & 80 - 60 = 20 & \frac{4}{20} = 0.2 \\ \hline \end{array}$$

Set up the linear scales and boundary ranges for the histogram on graph paper:
$$\begin{aligned}
\text{Horizontal axis (time)}: & \quad 0 \le t \le 80 \text{ minutes} \\
\text{Vertical axis (frequency density)}: & \quad 0 \le \text{FD} \le 1.8
\end{aligned}$$
Label the horizontal axis 'Time (mins)' and the vertical axis 'Frequency density'.

Plot each adjoining rectangular bar spanning the exact class boundaries with height equal to its frequency density:
$$\begin{aligned}
10 < t \le 25: & \quad \text{width} = 15, \quad \text{height} = 1.2 \\
25 < t \le 45: & \quad \text{width} = 20, \quad \text{height} = 1.6 \\
45 < t \le 60: & \quad \text{width} = 15, \quad \text{height} = 0.6 \\
60 < t \le 80: & \quad \text{width} = 20, \quad \text{height} = 0.2
\end{aligned}$$
Ensure all adjacent bars touch along the continuous time axis without gaps.

ai_rubric.Constructing Histograms: Draws bars with the stated class boundaries and correct frequency-density heights.
ai_rubric.Calculating Frequency Density: Uses frequency divided by class width for each histogram class.

teacher_walkthrough:
In a histogram, the height of each bar represents frequency density, calculated by dividing the class frequency by the class width:
$$\text{Frequency density} = \frac{\text{Frequency}}{\text{Class width}}$$

Calculate the width, frequency, and height for each interval:
- $10 < t \le 25$: width $= 15$, frequency $= 18$, height $= 18 / 15 = 1.2$
- $25 < t \le 45$: width $= 20$, frequency $= 32$, height $= 32 / 20 = 1.6$
- $45 < t \le 70$: width $= 25$, frequency $= 63 - 50 = 13$, height $= 13 / 25 = 0.52$
Plot the three adjacent bars on graph paper using these exact boundaries on the horizontal axis and heights on the vertical axis.

skill_tags: Estimating a Mean from Grouped Data

hints: Calculate the class midpoint $x = \dfrac{\text{lower bound} + \text{upper bound}}{2}$ for each non-empty time interval.
Multiply each midpoint by its class frequency to form the products $fx$.
Calculate $\sum fx$ and divide by the total frequency $n = 63$ to estimate the mean journey time.
walkthrough:
Find the midpoint $x$ of each non-empty time interval:
$$\begin{aligned}
10 < t \le 25: & \quad x_1 = \frac{10 + 25}{2} = 17.5 \\
25 < t \le 45: & \quad x_2 = \frac{25 + 45}{2} = 35.0 \\
45 < t \le 60: & \quad x_3 = \frac{45 + 60}{2} = 52.5 \\
60 < t \le 80: & \quad x_4 = \frac{60 + 80}{2} = 70.0
\end{aligned}$$

Compute the sum of products of class midpoints and frequencies, $\sum fx$:
$$\begin{aligned}
\sum fx &= (17.5 \times 18) + (35.0 \times 32) + (52.5 \times 9) + (70.0 \times 4) \\
&= 315 + 1120 + 472.5 + 280 \\
&= 2187.5
\end{aligned}$$

Divide $\sum fx$ by the total number of people $\sum f = 63$ to estimate the mean:
$$\bar{t} = \frac{\sum fx}{\sum f} = \frac{2187.5}{63} = 34.722... \approx 34.7 \text{ minutes}$$

ai_rubric.Estimating a Mean from Grouped Data: Uses class midpoints and frequencies in the grouped-mean calculation.

teacher_walkthrough:
To estimate the mean time, find the midpoint of each of the three class intervals:
$$\text{Midpoint of }(10, 25) = 17.5,\quad (25, 45) = 35,\quad (45, 70) = 57.5$$

Multiply each midpoint by the number of people in that group, and sum them to get the estimated total time:
$$\sum fx = (17.5 \times 18) + (35 \times 32) + (57.5 \times 13) = 315 + 1120 + 747.5 = 2182.5$$

Divide this total time by all 63 people to find the estimated mean:
$$\text{Estimated mean} = \frac{2182.5}{63} \approx 34.6\text{ minutes}$$
